breakaway_method: hold_gravity.py --dither-sweep, dither-hz 5: the dither amplitude at which a joint first shows >2 counts peak-to-peak IS its breakaway torque. Two runs at different poses; the all-joints run gave only LOWER BOUNDS for J1/J2 (they never moved) and is contaminated for the later joints because earlier ones broke loose and moved the arm, so the one-joint-at-a-time run is the better measurement. Stored values are the MINIMUM across runs (J1/J2 from the per-joint run, the only real numbers there), because the same joint varied by up to 1.9x between poses and OVER-compensation is the dangerous direction: feedforward above the local friction makes the joint self-driving. Keep kfric <= 0.7 so the 1.9x pose spread stays covered. static_friction_nm from identify_gravity.py under-reports all of this by roughly 5-14x and should not be used for gains.
gravity_fit_method: Refit 2026-09-20 with tools/piper/leader_gravity_id_collect.py data: 50 whole_v1 episodes replayed on the leader forward and backward at half speed. Averaging the two passes at the same path point cancels friction, so payload and per_joint_scale come from moving samples (|qd_ref| > 0.05 rad/s) with no offset term; J1 and J6 scale are pinned to 1.0 because their gravity torque is too small to identify one. 10 held-out episodes give the RMS below. static_friction_nm, breakaway_nm and their method note predate this and are unchanged; they came from the poses in friction_recording.
